tied to this tweet (https://t.co/LygmlouPhZ)

as an example, someone sent me a writeup on BAH...I dont know these businesses at all, but I have a cursory understanding of "the mkt thinks co's like ACN + peers, are in deep trouble bc of AI/LLMs."

so my first reply to the BAH pitch was, pull up price charts of all the peers and you can see it pretty fast (below)...you aren't making an idiosyncratic bet

the bet might be right (maybe BAH is okay and ACN isnt) but you gotta understand what battle you're fighting

your idea isn't down in a vacuum, its not "cheap bc its complex" or something tied to the biz in question, u have to understand + debunk the broad AI/LLM bear case

thats why these situations are hard, not just bc those are tough to debunk, but then you have to lay out "what is the event path/specific catalysts that will make the market view change + arrive at my variant view"

a lot of times, beating the next 2-3 qtrs doesn't change shit, bc that's not where the mkt is looking on the DCF...it knows 12-24 mo FCF is fine, it's concerned about "are LT EBIT margins 10% or 5%" or "is perp growth 5%, 0%, or (5%)?"

I have no opinion on whether these are the right battles to fight, but I don't think there's anything wrong with saying "fuck this" or tossing it into the "too hard" pile once u realize an idea is not what u thought it was.

helps parse out "do I actually have a fundamental, idiosyncratic idea here, or is this just some broad basket slash factor bet that I'm caught in." https://t.co/e9YrmqqYro
